segments.text: Maze, level six. We log in as maze six - level five's keygen paid off - and the goal is the maze7 password. The gate: /maze/maze6, setuid maze7, fourteen kilobytes, dynamically linked, with debug info.

This is a heap-forensics level and the working directory matters: /tmp is tmpfs nosuid, so everything happens in /run/screen, root's real filesystem. The exploit has three parts, all typed in vi. First the shellcode: sixty-nine bytes, open-read-write on /etc/maze_pass/maze7 - the path built with pushes in the same printable-chunk style as level two, and deliberately free of null bytes AND of the byte zero-x-two-a, because argv two goes through memfrob and a raw star would come back as a null.

Second, the builder. main overflows its buffer with an unbounded strcpy of argv two, then memfrobs it - xor forty-two, self-inverse - so the raw NULs in our payload ride in argv as star bytes and come back after the strlen. But main ends with exit, so the saved return address is dead. The win is the CALLER's frame, which the overflow reaches: repair argc, argv and envp pointers, relocate the argv array inside the payload, and replace the FILE pointer at buf plus zero-one-hundred with a byte-exact copy of the real heap FILE structure - a short copy misses the vtable at plus zero-ninety-four and glibc aborts. Point its write pointers at exit's GOT entry minus twenty-four, so main's own fprintf line is memcpy'd straight onto exit's GOT with the first four bytes being leave-ret. When exit runs, the GOT jump executes leave-ret: the stack pointer moves into our buffer and returns into the shellcode at buf plus zero-one-zero-eight.

Third, the driver: w-six-dot-py loads the builder, sweeps the buffer address over a two-kilobyte band of the stack inside the live session's own environment - the address is env-dependent, gdb measured zero-x-f-f-f-f-d-eight-twenty-four under a different layout - and fires the level for each candidate. The hit lands at zero-x-f-f-f-f-c-f-c-four, the same address as the original session, and the password prints: c-k-K-O-x-two-s-four-E-v, read straight from the maze7 password file by the shellcode's write.

Verification: exit the session and log in fresh as maze seven with that password - the cast reaches the maze7 prompt, and the replay below completes the check: u i d fifteen thousand seven, cat /etc/maze_pass/maze7 shows the same string. Maze six done.
